name: Dumbbell Straight-Arm Pullover
description: The dumbbell straight-arm pullover is a classic exercise that places a deep stretch on the chest and lats as the arms arc behind the head. When performed with a focus on the chest and ribs flaring, it stimulates the sternal head of the pectoralis major and the serratus anterior in a range of motion not achievable with most pressing movements.

execution.starting_position: Lie across a flat bench with only your upper back and shoulders supported. Hold a single dumbbell by one end with both hands, arms extended above the chest.
execution.setup_instructions: Position yourself perpendicular or along the bench so your upper back is supported. Hips may hang lower than the bench. Grasp the dumbbell with both hands overlapping around the top weight plate.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms extended above your chest, slight bend at the elbows.
Step 2: Slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head, keeping the arms as straight as possible.
Step 3: Lower until a stretch is felt through the chest and lats, typically when the arms are parallel to the floor or slightly below.
Step 4: Squeeze the chest and arc the dumbbell back over the face to the starting position.
Step 5: Focus on a smooth, controlled arc — not a pulldown.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale as you lower the dumbbell behind your head. Exhale as you return it to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows too much, turning it into a triceps extension
Going too heavy and losing control at the bottom
Dropping the hips during the movement
safety_considerations: Avoid this exercise with any shoulder impingement or injury
Use a moderate weight — excessive load stresses the glenohumeral joint
Keep the core engaged to prevent lower back arching
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lower the dumbbell until a comfortable chest and lat stretch is achieved. Never force the arms past a point of shoulder discomfort.
coaching_cues: Breathe deeply as you lower — let the ribcage expand
Feel the stretch from armpit to armpit
Drive the dumbbell back with the chest, not the arms
